newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo low-grown tea prices fall on Gulf fears.
newsitem.headline: Colombo low-grown tea prices fall on Gulf fears.

text.p: Sri Lankan low-grown tea prices fell at Wednesday's auction as U.S.-Iraq tensions unnerved buyers, brokers said.

"Low-growns came down on speculation," said a broker. "Buyers do not want to buy in case war breaks out and shipping is disrupted in the Middle East. Then they'll get landed with stock which is quite expensive to carry."
Brokers Forbes and Walker said the anticipated gross auction average price for the 4.5 million kg on offer should rise to 121.25 rupees per kg from 119.33 rupees per kg last week.
Brokers said they believed the market had peaked.
"We've seen the end of the Uva quality season," said another broker. "The market is now on the way down although individual grades might move up."
The next auction is on September 17-18 where 4.3 million kg will be on offer.
